verses.text: They brought in God’s ark, and set it in the middle of the tent that David had pitched for it; and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.
When David had finished offering the burnt offering and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in Yahweh’s name.
He gave to everyone of Israel, both man and woman, to everyone a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins.
He appointed some of the Levites to minister before Yahweh’s ark, and to commemorate, to thank, and to praise Yahweh, the God of Israel:

Asaph the chief, and second to him Zechariah, then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel, with stringed instruments and with harps; and Asaph with cymbals, sounding aloud;
with Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests with trumpets continually, before the ark of the covenant of God.
Then on that day David first ordained to give thanks to Yahweh, by the hand of Asaph and his brothers.
Oh give thanks to Yahweh. Call on his name. Make what he has done known among the peoples.
Sing to him. Sing praises to him. Tell of all his marvelous works.
Glory in his holy name. Let the heart of those who seek Yahweh rejoice.
Seek Yahweh and his strength. Seek his face forever more.
Remember his marvelous works that he has done, his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth,
you offspring  of Israel his servant, you children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
He is Yahweh our God. His judgments are in all the earth.
Remember his covenant forever, the word which he commanded to a thousand generations,
the covenant which he made with Abraham, his oath to Isaac.
He confirmed the same to Jacob for a statute, and to Israel for an everlasting covenant,
saying, “I will give you the land of Canaan, The lot of your inheritance,”
when you were but a few men in number, yes, very few, and foreigners were in it.
They went about from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.
He allowed no man to do them wrong. Yes, he reproved kings for their sakes,
“Don’t touch my anointed ones! Do my prophets no harm!”
Sing to Yahweh, all the earth! Display his salvation from day to day.
Declare his glory among the nations, and his marvelous works among all the peoples.
For great is Yahweh, and greatly to be praised. He also is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but Yahweh made the heavens.
Honor and majesty are before him. Strength and gladness are in his place.
Ascribe to Yahweh, you relatives of the peoples, ascribe to Yahweh glory and strength!
Ascribe to Yahweh the glory due to his name. Bring an offering, and come before him. Worship Yahweh in holy array.
Tremble before him, all the earth. The world also is established that it can’t be moved.
Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice! Let them say among the nations, “Yahweh reigns!”
Let the sea roar, and its fullness! Let the field exult, and all that is in it!
Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before Yahweh, for he comes to judge the earth.
Oh give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever.
Say, “Save us, God of our salvation! Gather us together and deliver us from the nations, to give thanks to your holy name, to triumph in your praise.”
Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, from everlasting even to everlasting.  All the people said, “Amen,” and praised Yahweh.
So he left Asaph and his brothers there before the ark of Yahweh’s covenant, to minister before the ark continually, as every day’s work required;
and Obed-Edom with their brothers, sixty-eight; Obed-Edom also the son of Jeduthun and Hosah to be doorkeepers;
and Zadok the priest, and his brothers the priests, before Yahweh’s tabernacle in the high place that was at Gibeon,
to offer burnt offerings to Yahweh on the altar of burnt offering continually morning and evening, even according to all that is written in Yahweh’s law, which he commanded to Israel;
and with them Heman and Jeduthun, and the rest who were chosen, who were mentioned by name, to give thanks to Yahweh, because his loving kindness endures forever;
and with them Heman and Jeduthun with trumpets and cymbals for those that should sound aloud, and with instruments for the songs of God; and the sons of Jeduthun to be at the gate.
All the people departed, each man to his house; and David returned to bless his house.

footnotes.content: David has carried the ark into the tent he pitched—a place of honor, set apart. He offers burnt offerings for atonement, peace offerings for gratitude, both. Sometimes our worship is most true when we remember we come as sinners first, then as grateful children.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David blesses the people in Yahweh's name, not his own. That's the mark of a true shepherd—he knows his blessing is only the Lord's overflow through him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A loaf, a portion of meat, a cake of raisins—the same share to man and woman alike. David's table mirrors the equality of the Lord's table, where every soul is equally treasured.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David appoints Levites to minister before the ark—to commemorate, thank, and praise. He saw that worship itself is holy work, and set aside people for it. What we make time for shows what we truly believe matters.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Asaph and his brothers with strings and harps, cymbals sounding loud—names, instruments, places. They're not hidden in the crowd but named, known, their gifts on display. The Lord sees the faithful ones who raise the song.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Priests with trumpets continually before the ark—not once, but as a rhythm, a steady call. Some worship is one moment; some is a faithful returning, day after day.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David ordinates thanksgiving—he makes it official, a practice, not a mood. He understood that we need to command joy to its place, not wait for it to arrive.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Give thanks. Call on his name. Make what he has done known. Three simple commands that ripple out—into the heart, into prayer, into witness. Praise is both private and public, both mine and theirs.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sing and sing and tell—the same truth in three forms. Sometimes singing says what words alone cannot. Sometimes we need to sing before we can speak it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Glory in his holy name—let those seeking him have their hearts set on fire with joy. The Lord's character is not grim or distant; it kindles gladness in the soul that turns toward it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seek his face forever more—not just once, but a lifetime posture. To seek the Lord's face is to want to know him, to come into his presence. That hunger, that forever-reaching, is the whole of the spiritual life.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Remember his marvelous works—we forget so easily. Remembering is how faith lives; forgetting is how it dies. To hold his works in mind is to hold his character in your heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You offspring of Israel, children of Jacob—the chosen ones. Not because they were better, but because they were claimed. That same chosenness reaches through time to us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His judgments are in all the earth—not just in Scripture or temple, but everywhere. To see the Lord's justice, mercy, and order woven through the world itself is to see him constantly at work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A thousand generations—the Lord thinks in timescales we can barely imagine. He does not make promises for today or tomorrow only, but stakes them across centuries.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The covenant with Abraham, the oath to Isaac—names and relationships, specific promises to specific men. God does not make vague commitments; he binds himself to his people by name.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A statute for Jacob, an everlasting covenant for Israel—what God swears, he confirms. He did not leave his promise on a note; he made it law, written into the fabric of relationship.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will give you the land—direct and clear. The Lord announces what he will do, and does it. Our faith grows when we learn to believe the simplicity of his word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Few men in number, foreigners in the land—Israel began as a minority, as outsiders. That humility was their strength. The Lord chooses the small and makes them vast.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They went about from nation to nation—wanderers, without a home. Yet they were never lost; the Lord went with them. Sometimes our own wandering seasons teach us most deeply that he never lets us go.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He allowed no man to do them wrong—the Lord is a fierce defender of his people, reproves kings for their sake. There is a tenderness in the Father; he cannot bear to see his own mistreated.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't touch my anointed ones—a warning wrapped in love. The Lord's servants carry his authority; to harm them is to lay a hand on him. We are far more protected than we know.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sing to Yahweh, all the earth—not just the faithful few, but all. The invitation to praise is universal; every creature is invited to join the song.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Declare his glory among the nations—witness spreads not through force but through declaration. Tell what you have seen; let others see it too.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Great is Yahweh and greatly to be praised, yet also to be feared—praise and reverence are not opposed. The deeper we love him, the more we stand in awe of his holiness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the gods of the peoples are idols, but Yahweh made the heavens—the contrast is stark. Dead stone versus the living Creator. To worship anything else is to bow to emptiness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Honor and majesty are before him, strength and gladness in his place—to draw near the Lord is to step into magnificence and joy at once. His throne is not terrible only; it is radiant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ascribe to Yahweh, you relatives of the peoples—not strangers, but family. Even outsiders are beckoned into kinship with the Lord's family.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bring an offering, come before him, worship in holy array—worship is not casual. We dress it in our best, bring our gifts, approach with reverence. The Lord receives what we give with full hearts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tremble before him—the world itself trembles. When we step into the presence of the Almighty, fear is the proper first response. Yet that fear is the doorway to safety.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Let the heavens be glad, let the earth rejoice, let them say Yahweh reigns—all creation joins the chorus. Joy and reign go together; where Christ is Lord, there is gladness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Let the sea roar, the field exult, all that is in it—nature itself is invited to praise. The mountains know his glory; the waters tell it. We are not alone in our song.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The trees of the forest sing for joy—he comes to judge the earth. That judgment is not dread alone; it is the promise that wrongs will be set right, that justice will come.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Give thanks, for he is good—goodness is his nature, not his mood. When we struggle to be grateful, we can return to this anchor: he is good, always.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Save us, gather us, deliver us—David's plea lifts the burden from the people's shoulders. We do not save ourselves; we call on the God of our salvation and rest in his deliverance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Blessed be Yahweh from everlasting to everlasting, all the people said Amen—the psalm closes in unison. When a congregation says Amen together, they pledge their hearts to what was sung. That single word is a covenant spoken aloud.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Asaph and his brothers left to minister continually, as every day's work required—faithfulness is not a burst of fervor but a daily showing up. The Lord honors the ordinary, faithful servant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Obed-Edom and brothers, doorkeepers—every role matters. The ones at the door keep the sanctuary, a sacred trust. Not all of us are called to sing from the center; some are called to guard the threshold.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zadok the priest at Gibeon—David ensured the old sanctuary was still tended while the ark had a new home. He honored what was established while embracing what was new.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Burnt offerings morning and evening, according to all that is written in Yahweh's law—order and regularity ground the faith. The rhythms of obedience shape us in ways one grand gesture never could.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The chosen ones, mentioned by name, because his loving kindness endures forever—we are known. We are named. And it is his mercy that keeps us, not our strength.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Heman and Jeduthun with trumpets and cymbals, instruments for the songs of God—music is not decoration but a form of prayer, a language the heart speaks when words fall short.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the people departed, each to his house; David returned to bless his house—readers today hear an echo: a shepherd goes home to his own people carrying the weight of blessing them. Jesus did the same—carried the burdens, fed the flock, then returned to the Father's house. The pattern is ancient and it is forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
